01 DATA
TO DECISION
Dataset→Clean→Engineer→Split→Compare→Evaluate

The question How well can incident-time location, weather and road context classify traffic-impact severity, from level 1 to level 4?

The source US Accidents, March 2023 release. One row describes one reported incident. Severity measures traffic disruption; it does not measure injury severity.

03 / FEATURE ENGINEERING

Turn context into signals.

Deterministic rules derive time, road and weather features from each incident.

The same incidents, richer context.

Match the incident IDs across both tables. These values come from the actual cleaning function.

Select the final model inputs.

After deriving features, retain the explicit predictor list and traceability metadata. End time, extent and narrative are excluded. Severity is the target; ID and Source are never predictors. ID appears below only to match incidents.

04 / SPLIT & ENCODING

Keep the test set unseen.

Split after cleaning and deduplication. Learn preprocessing only from the fitting partition.

First, deduplicate across the full archive.

Cleaning and feature engineering run per chunk. Once all chunks are processed, the pipeline keeps the first event with an exact local start time and original-precision coordinates, across all providers. Only then does it split the retained rows.

Different groups of actual removed and retained preview rows, verified against the saved full-data manifest. Coincident independent incidents may be merged by this conservative rule.

Development → selection → refit

Saved row assignments

Real memberships from the saved split. Tuning and validation are subsets of development.

From categories to model inputs.

The saved LightGBM encoder maps training categories to codes. City and County are qualified with State. Codes are marked categorical, not interpreted as a ranking. Missing numeric values remain missing; unseen categories map to −1.

The logistic regression comparison instead fits numeric medians, missingness indicators, scaling and one-hot encoding on its fitting data.

Example codes come from the final encoder fitted on development data. Candidate selection used its own fitting-only encoder.

    TRY THE TRAINED MODEL

    Your inputs. A new prediction.

    Describe an incident to predict its traffic-impact severity, from level 1 to level 4.

    The strongest signals come first. Location, date, road type and traffic signals lead this form because they rank highest in the saved validation results. The date supplies year, month, hour and weekday automatically.

    Why these inputs?

    Ranked by the drop in macro F1 when each feature is shuffled on 12,000 validation records. One repeat; related features can share importance.
